questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to improve my German as well as the chance to get to know a European capital with a rich cultural history

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Covid naturally had an impact but I still enjoyed my stay and had a lot of great experiences

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The website of the University of Vienna was very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I used the university's website to find information and also received some tips and help from my Erasmus network buddy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
Pros: The coordinator at the institute of mathematics was very helpful whenever I e-mailed a question.
Cons: The university's website was not up-to-date with information regarding covid. The international office did not respond to e-mails even though this was the only way they could be contacted according to the website.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy to find accomodation at the OeAD student housing, though only some of their dorms were available by the time I applied (2 months before arrival).
However, I would recommend instead looking for a room in a shared flat, seeing how that tends to be cheaper than student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I will recommend living close to the 7th district

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The OeAD dorms are not the best places to live but it is a very convenient way of finding accomodation

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course catalogue was somewhat confusing as it is finalized very close to the beginning of the semester and because two different curricula for the mathematics programme were in use at the same time, which was not immediately obvious from the website.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses online. Do note that lectures and exercise classes are treated as separate courses so you will need to register for each of them separately. For lectures, you are guaranteed to be able to attend, while exercise classes have limited space.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contcated the Erasmus coordinator at my institute via e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One course was cancelled entirely with short notice before the start of the semester. Aside from that, I was allowed to attend all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can register for any number of courses, in case you do not get a space in all your desired courses, and then deregister once spaces have been allocated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a wide selection of courses, though the summer semester seemed to have more options, and most of my courses were very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I followed mostly BA courses and found the teaching slightly more demanding than at UCPH though the exams were more forgiving.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference is that in most courses, you are graded for your participation in exercise classes where you will usually be required to succesfully present a few exercises per course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Complex Analysis, Numeric Mathematics, Introduction to Mathematical Logic (MA course), Mathematics Meets Philosophy, and Gender Aspects of Mathematics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Complex Analysis was my favorite course. Introduction to Mathematical Logic was very interesting but also incredibly challenging - however, the lecturers/teachers for this course were great.
Mathematics Meets Philosophy is too easy (compared to VtMat at UCPH) and Gender Aspects of Mathematics was unfortunately also a somewhat disappointing course.

questions.answer: None, really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most courses do not require the purchase of any books. Public transportation is really cheap (75 euro per semester). Cinemas are cheap!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The selection of sports and other activities for students is great; however you have to be very quick to sign up

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports as well as some music and performance classes offered by the university sports institute.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not personally attend any uni sports but it sounded great

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go hiking on the Stadtwanderwege. Get very cheap tickets (~90% discount if you're <27 years old) for operas with the app Gretchen and go to concerts and plays. Go to museums; buy an annual ticket for Kunsthistorisches Museum (which is worth several visits by itself) which also gives access to a few small museums. The Ephesos Museum is great for ancient history. MUMOK, Albertina (main one as well as Albertina Modern) and Upper Belvedere were my favorite art museums.
The 7th district in particular has a LOT of nice cafés and bars.
It'es easy to go on trips to for example Budapest or other towns in Austria. Schneeberg is a nice place to go hiking, easily reached by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I didn't really experience any culture clash

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Stores are closed on Sundays

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sitting in a café for hours (while studying, for example)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) It is very easy to meet other Erasmus students. Sign up for welcome events and WhatsApp group chats with other students in order to meet people
2) Do seek out as many cultural experiences as you have the time for (they are endless)
3) If you want to meet local people, seek them out through hobbies and such

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can get by in the city without speaking particularly good German

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with other Erasmus students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Finding for both studying, social events as well as pursuing hobbies
Also, practicing German rather than defaulting to speaking in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
